items.title: UAPA does not bar bail merely because accused is a foreign national: Supreme Court
items.summary: The Supreme Court on Tuesday held that an accused’s foreign nationality alone does not bar the grant of bail under the Unlawful Activities (Prevention) Act (UAPA) [Union of India v. Mohamed Rifas ]. A Bench of Justices Aravind Kumar and Vipul M Pancholi clarified that the bail restriction under Section 43D(7) of UAPA applies only if the foreign national also entered India illegally or without authorisation. “ Merely because a person is not an Indian Citizen will not suffice to trigger the rigors of sub-section (7) of Section 43D, ” the Court held. It explained that a foreign national’s lawful entry into India does not become unlawful merely because their authorisation is subsequently revoked or their stay becomes illegal. “ What is required and necessary is that when such person entered India initially, such entrance itself was unauthorised or illegal, ” the Court said. items.title: Instagram account block by Meta has to be challenged by way of civil suit, not writ petition: Delhi High Court
items.summary: The Delhi High Court has held that a writ petition seeking restoration of an Instagram account is not maintainable against Meta Platforms [Sarthak Bhagat v Union of India & Ors] . Justice Amit Mahajan held that Meta does not perform a public function or discharge a public duty, which are the conditions necessary to maintain a writ under Article 226 of the Constitution of India. Hence, blocking of Instagram account by Meta has to be challenged by way of a civil suit and not a writ petition, the Court said. The Court explained that while Instagram plays a significant role in disseminating information and shaping public opinion, its primary function is to provide a platform for expression, with public discourse being a consequence of its operations rather than a public duty. “Its operations remain private in nature, and no governmental mandate delegates any traditional State function to it. Respondent No. 3 [Meta] is neither obligated to provide such a platform in discharge of a public duty nor legally compelled to offer its services, which are voluntary and user-driven.
